T: Old trees, taller than anything in the Archive. The air smells of rain and pine.
F: A split-rail fence, grey with age. Someone mends it now and then.
S: A signpost. One arm reads ONWARD, pointing east. The other arm has been snapped off.
Behind the post, the trees don't quite meet.
c: A candle in an iron lantern, burning steadily at the roadside. It feels like the Archive's candles. Somehow, it feels safe.
J: A cocoon, half hidden in the long grass at the roadside. A leather satchel strap pokes out of the silk.
Whoever is inside was going somewhere in a hurry.
The silk won't give. Not yet.
=: The great door of the Archive, set into a hill of old stone. From out here, it looks like it has always been part of the hill.
>: The road runs on east toward distant towers.
H: The Waystation. Smoke curls from its chimney, and a painted sign over the door shows a running boot.
L: A strip of old leather, snagged on a low branch: a satchel strap, cracked with age.
Tucked behind it, a folded page in a careful, hurried hand:
"If I don't make it back, the letter still goes. A courier doesn't read the post. A courier delivers it."
<: The road runs west, toward the smell of turnips.

lines: HALT! Nobody passes without a duel!
...Unless you're going the other way. Then carry on. Mind the puddle.

answer: Nobody. I watch the grass. The wind shoves it flat, and it gets back up.
That's the whole secret. Don't tell anyone. Especially the grass.
Towers. Mum says a king lives there who never gets any older.
I asked if that's because he eats his greens. She said not to ask that loudly.
There's a lady asleep in the long grass, all wrapped up. She looks like she's still running.
I leave her a flower sometimes. Runners get tired.

lines: A brass plaque by the Waystation: REST HERE, COURIER. THE ROAD REMEMBERS EVERY RUNNER.
Under the words, a running boot, worn almost smooth by passing hands.
Half-buried in the grass: the signpost's missing arm. The paint reads ...ECREST.
Whatever it pointed to, it's pointing at the dirt now.
In the hollow of an old pine, out of the rain: a Heart Piece, wrapped in a courier's glove.
Wedged in the roots below the torn strap: a letter in oilcloth, dry after all this time.
The seal is unbroken. A courier doesn't read the post. You decide you won't either.
